# Complexity Thresholds and Enforcement

Dimension covering recommended cyclomatic complexity limits from standards
bodies, industry practitioners, and Python tooling.

Sources: see [citations.md](../citations.md) for full details.

## Threshold Comparison

| Source | Threshold | Year | Context |
|--------|-----------|------|---------|
| McCabe (original) [1] | 10 | 1976 | Split modules exceeding this |
| NIST SP 500-235 [2][3] | 10 (up to 15) | 1996 | 15 requires operational advantages |
| NASA SWEHB [6] | 10-15 | — | Safety-critical software |
| Code Complete (McConnell) [30] | 10 hard, 6-10 warning | 2004 | Most conservative mainstream |
| C4/CMU Reference Guide [29] | 20 (default) | 1997 | With 4-tier risk classification |
| NDepend [7] | 15+ warning, 30+ critical | — | .NET ecosystem |
| Microsoft CA1502 [3] | 25 | — | Visual Studio code analysis |
| Mark Seemann [22] | 7 | 2019 | Based on cognitive load research |
| mccabe (Python) [8] | 10 | 2022 | De facto Python standard |
| lizard [13] | 15 | 2026 | Multi-language default |
| radon Grade B ceiling [10] | 10 | — | B grade = 6-10 |

## The NIST Position

The authoritative statement on thresholds comes from NIST SP 500-235 (Watson &
McCabe, 1996), reproduced verbatim by Microsoft Learn [3]:

> "The precise number to use as a limit, however, remains somewhat
> controversial. The original limit of 10 as proposed by McCabe has significant
> supporting evidence, but limits as high as 15 have been used successfully as
> well. Limits over 10 should be reserved for projects that have several
> operational advantages over typical projects, for example experienced staff,
> formal design, a modern programming language, structured programming, code
> walkthroughs, and a comprehensive test plan." [2][3]

## NASA and Safety-Critical Standards

NASA's Software Engineering Handbook states that "cyclomatic complexity for
safety-critical software should typically remain below 10-15" — presented as a
rule of thumb, not an absolute regulatory requirement [6].

Enforcement mechanisms [6]:
1. Coding standards compliance (MISRA-C, CERT-C, NASA-specific guidelines)
2. Automated monitoring with thresholds during coding and code review
3. Peer review with complexity reduction as explicit focus
4. Independent verification teams for high-complexity code

Regulatory references: NPR 7150.2, DO-178C, MISRA [6].

## NASA SATC: Complexity + Size

The NASA Software Assurance Technology Center found that neither complexity nor
size alone is sufficient [27][3]:

> "The SATC has found the most effective evaluation is a combination of size and
> (Cyclomatic) complexity. The modules with both a high complexity and a large
> size tend to have the lowest reliability. Modules with low size and high
> complexity are also a reliability risk because they tend to be very terse code,
> which is difficult to change or modify." [27]

## Python Tool Defaults

| Tool | Default | Enabled by Default? |
|------|---------|---------------------|
| mccabe (flake8) [8] | 10 | No (use --max-complexity) |
| ruff C901 [16] | 10 | No (add C901 to select) |
| lizard [13] | 15 | Yes |
| pytest-mccabe [28] | 15 (in config example) | No (use --mccabe) |
| xenon [11] | Letter grades (A-F) | N/A (manual threshold) |

**Python consensus**: 10 is the standard threshold. The mccabe package
explicitly states: "According to McCabe, anything that goes beyond 10 is too
complex" [8]. Ruff defaults to the same value [16].

## Radon Grading Scale

Radon maps CC scores to letter grades [10]:

| Grade | CC Range | Practical Meaning |
|-------|----------|-------------------|
| A     | 1-5      | Simple, easy to test |
| B     | 6-10     | Within McCabe's limit |
| C     | 11-20    | Exceeds McCabe, within NIST relaxation |
| D     | 21-30    | High risk per C4 classification |
| E     | 31-40    | Very high risk |
| F     | 41+      | Untestable per McCabe's risk categories |

Xenon uses these grades for enforcement: `--max-absolute=B` means no function
may exceed CC 10 [11][12].

## Enforcement Strategies

**Hard gate**: Block merges when threshold exceeded. Tools: xenon (non-zero
exit), ruff/flake8 (CI linting step) [8][11][16].

**Warning only**: Report violations without blocking. Tools: radon (-nc flag
to show C-grade or worse), wily (diff reports) [9][14].

**Trend monitoring**: Track complexity over time, alert on regressions. Tool:
wily (git-history-based analysis) [14].

**Per-file exceptions**: Allow higher thresholds for specific files. Tool:
pytest-mccabe (glob-based overrides in setup.cfg) [28].

## Gaps and Limitations

- No Python-specific threshold research found — all recommendations derive
  from language-agnostic studies (primarily C, Java)
- No empirical data on the costs (velocity impact) of enforcing strict
  thresholds in Python projects
- SonarQube's Python CC threshold was not confirmed from primary documentation
